# Interpretation — #568: Third orthogonal source pair at the mid dial (round 1)

## Headline

**Hypothesis FALSIFIED on the position read; envelope membership SPLIT.** All three new joint cells (navy_seal × french_person at band [9, 13]) land at GD1 effective rank ~1.38 — far above the pre-registered success band (1.2753, 1.3111), above every single one of the 18 anchor joint cells (max 1.3355 at #527), and above the upper KILL edge of the pre-registered tolerance ring [1.2613, 1.3201] (3-cell mean = 1.3792, +0.0591 ≈ +3.7 within-dial-SD above the kill edge). The pre-registered three-way verdict partition fires **KILL** cleanly: trigger B (3-cell mean outside [1.2613, 1.3201]) fires; trigger A (≥2/3 cells past the buffered envelope ≤1.15 or ≥1.50) does NOT fire — none of the 3 cells crosses 1.50, so the new pair sits in a "softly outside the cluster, well inside the buffered envelope" regime that the partition was built to call KILL on the cluster axis without overclaiming a recipe break on the envelope axis. The continuous regression-residual read agrees: each new cell sits +4.7 to +5.7 within-dial-SD ABOVE the 18-anchor anchor-line, mean +5.30 SD.

The dial-axis "small monotone gradient generalizes" claim from #550 does NOT widen to a third pair at the level of the GD1 cluster position. The envelope-membership claim splits: GD1 effective rank stays inside [1.20, 1.40] on all 3 cells (but barely — 1.3826 sits 0.0174 below the upper edge); GD1 top-1 SV share fails [0.85, 0.91] on 2 of 3 cells (0.8476, 0.8482, with 0.8522 the lone inside-band reading). GD3 worse-of-pair effective rank fails [1.20, 1.40] on ALL 3 cells (1.416, 1.424, 1.429).

**Confidence: LOW** on a "the gradient doesn't generalize" headline (n = 3 cells, 1 new pair, single dial; the result is consistent with either pair-specific geometry OR a pair-type confound — profession × nationality vs the two profession × profession anchors — that the design cannot disentangle). **MODERATE** on the narrower descriptive claim "the GD1 cluster position is not transferable across pairs without a pair term" — this part survives a 5-sigma residual, all 3 seeds agree, all 3 cells fire band-stop in [9, 13] at matched landings, source-side implant strength is matched to anchors, and the pre-registered partition fires cleanly. The KILL verdict on the position axis is not noise.

## Reads beyond the partition (descriptive)

1. **Source implant strength is matched to anchors.** Source Δlog P(marker) for navy_seal across the 3 joint cells: 9.40, 9.52, 9.57 nat. For french_person: 10.16, 10.22, 10.63 nat. The #550 anchors' joint-cell source Δlog P sat in 8.4–10.7 nat; the new pair is squarely in the same range. The implant landed on the dial as designed; the geometry it produced is the deviant.

2. **DV1 additivity is healthy.** Per-context DV1 median 0.994-0.996, identical to the anchor-pair distribution. The near-orthogonality (|cos| = 0.0150, vs +0.0012 and −0.0040 for the two existing pairs) still licenses the sum decomposition shift_{A+B} ≈ shift_A + shift_B at the L20 post-response slot. The KILL is NOT an additivity break — it is a same-additivity, higher-rank geometry. This is informative: it rules out one of the more obvious mechanistic stories ("less orthogonal source pairs share fewer dimensions, so the sum requires more rank to represent").

3. **Bystander leakage is LOWER, not higher.** Bystander Δlog P median per joint cell: new pair 6.378, 6.365, 6.508 nat (median ~6.4). #550 reference: 8.222, 9.899, 9.339, 9.391, 7.770, 7.997 nat (median ~8.7). The new pair leaks ~2 nat LESS to bystanders than the #550 anchors at matched source strength and matched landing — even though its joint-shift geometry uses MORE rank. This cuts against any naive "more rank = more leakage" story; the per-context shift is using more independent directions but the marker mass it deposits on bystanders is smaller. Two plausible reads, neither distinguishable here: (a) the navy_seal and french_person directions in shift space happen to be farther from the 17 bystanders' directions than the florist/medical_doctor or librarian/police_officer directions are from their bystanders; (b) the GD1 inflation lives largely in directions the bystander personas don't sit on, so the rank goes up without the bystander projection going up. The figure caption notes this; a clean follow-up could partial bystander Δlog P on pair-bystander cosine to test (a).

4. **Old-sources-as-bystanders read.** The 4 anchor sources (florist, medical_doctor, librarian, police_officer) are bystanders here. Their Δlog P in the new joint cells reads ~6-7 nat (similar to the other 13 true bystanders) — no inherited-marker signature, no privileged-direction leakage. The new pair did not learn anything special about the old sources.

5. **Stop steps differ.** Joint cells stopped at step 55 across all 3 seeds. Singleton stops: A_only 45/40/45; B_only 40/40/40. ## What this is and isn't

**Is:** a clean falsification of the narrow predictive claim "the GD1 cluster position transfers across pairs at matched dial settings" on the very first test. The pre-registered partition was deliberately built to call KILL on a deviation of this size (the ring [1.2613, 1.3201] is wider than every observed per-pair anchor cluster mean — and the new pair sits 0.06 above it); the continuous residual read confirms (+5.3 SD on the mean); the source-strength + landing checks rule out under-/over-training as the cause.

**Isn't:** a recipe break, an envelope break (the eff-rank envelope [1.20, 1.40] still holds), an additivity break (DV1 is fine), or a leakage-mode break (bystander emission stays at 0 and Δlog P is lower, not higher).

**Carries one structural confound the design cannot resolve.** navy_seal × french_person is profession × nationality vs two profession × profession anchors — KILL/GRAY readings cannot distinguish "pair-specific" from "pair-type-specific" geometry. The follow-up either way is the same: widen the pair panel (more pairs, ideally including more nationality / role-type mixes, at this dial) before any recipe-level conclusion about the dial-axis gradient. Per the planner's §11 critic-ensemble note 8, the appropriate framing is "level prediction does not transfer across pairs without a pair term," not "the gradient claim is wrong" — the 18 anchor cells still show a small monotone gradient WITHIN each of the two existing pairs across the dial; this run says only that a third pair sits OFF the joint mean across all dials.

**The |cos| = 0.0150 relaxation.** Per the named scope caveat from the plan §-deviations, the new pair's |cos| is 4-13× the two existing pairs' (0.0012, 0.0040) — well below the matrix's typical scale and 10× under the #527 selector's threshold, but still a real difference.
